subject: HIPAA eligibility & BAA — scope and PHI handling
messages:
From: Eliza Hoover <eliza.hoover@northstar-health.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 16:14:00 +0000
Subject: HIPAA / BAA — Redwood eligibility and PHI handling

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the product demo last week. NorthStar is interested in moving forward with Redwood for a patient-facing feature that will ingest and analyze short clinical notes. Before we proceed to procurement we need to confirm a couple of HIPAA-related items so our legal and compliance teams can assess eligibility: 

- Are you able to sign a Business Associate Agreement (BAA) with NorthStar? If so, do you have a standard BAA we can review?
- Which deployment modes are allowed for PHI? Can we send PHI to the hosted API, or is Dedicated / Private required?
- Do you support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for encryption at rest and in transit?
- What logs are retained by Redwood and could they contain PHI in plain text (request/response bodies, cache, or operational logs)?
- Do you have an SOC 2 Type II report and any HIPAA/PHI-specific controls documentation?

We need answers in the next two weeks for our vendor review. If you can share a draft BAA and some high-level technical notes (encryption, logging, key management, subprocessor list) that would help accelerate the review.

Eliza Hoover
Director of Vendor Risk — NorthStar Health
eliza.hoover@northstar-health.com
+1 415-555-0147

Note: I copied our Legal alias for the review: legal@northstar-health.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Eliza Hoover <eliza.hoover@northstar-health.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 20:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: HIPAA / BAA — Redwood eligibility and PHI handling

Hi Eliza — great to hear from you and thanks for the clear list. High level answers below, and I attached our standard BAA template (BAA_Template_Redwood_v1.pdf) for Legal to review. Happy to hop on a call with you and your legal/compliance team.

- BAA: Yes, Redwood will sign a BAA for customers using deployments that process PHI. Attached is our standard template; we’re open to reasonable redlines and a quick turnaround.
- Deployment modes: Our hosted multi-tenant API is not intended for PHI. For HIPAA workloads we require either Redwood Dedicated (single-tenant reserved capacity) or Redwood Private (VPC / on-prem) depending on your isolation and network needs.
- Key management: Dedicated and Private deployments can be configured with customer-managed KMS integrations; Private can support on-prem HSMs where required.
- Logs & PHI: We can configure request/response redaction and prefix/KV caching rules to avoid storing PHI in logs or caches. By default, application-level payloads are not persisted in cleartext in operational logs, but we will confirm specifics and provide an attestable control list.
- SOC 2: We maintain SOC 2 Type II; I included a link to the most recent report in related links. We also have a security questionnaire pack we can share (SIG/CAIQ relevant sections).

Next steps I propose:
1) Your Legal reviews the attached BAA and returns any redlines (we can accept DocuSign).
2) Technical call with your cloud/compliance team and our infra/security engineer (Rishi) to go over KMS, logging, and retention.
3) We’ll produce a short written walkthrough of the PHI handling flow for your review.

I’m available Wed/Thu mornings PT for a 30-min call.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Healthcare
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (650) 555-0199

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 14:28:00 +0000
Subject: Internal: technical notes for NorthStar — KMS, logs, retention

Marissa / Dev — posting a concise list you can share with NorthStar Legal/Tech. Copy/paste friendly.

1) Model I/O and PHI:
   - We strongly recommend that any PHI-containing input/output be processed on Redwood Dedicated or Private. Hosted (multi-tenant) is not HIPAA-approved and should not be used for PHI.

2) Encryption & Key Management:
   - In transit: TLS 1.2+ always enforced.
   - At rest: AES-256. For Dedicated and Private we support customer-managed keys through AWS KMS / Azure Key Vault / GCP KMS. For Private on-prem deployments we can integrate with HSMs.

3) Logs, caches, and persistence:
   - Application logs: configurable to redact request/response bodies. Default logging omits full payloads; operational traces may include metadata only.
   - KV cache / prefix caching: can be disabled or configured per-customer to avoid caching PHI.
   - Persistent storage: model weights and runtime artifacts are never stored with customer data. Customer data retention window configurable; default retention for Dedicated: 30 days after processed, with secure deletion on request.

4) Auditability & Monitoring:
   - Detailed access logs (who, when, action) retained and exportable for audit.
   - Support for SIEM integration and S3 log export for forensic review.

5) Subprocessors & breach notification:
   - We maintain a subprocessors list; subprocessors handling PHI will be identified in the BAA.
   - We commit to notification timelines: initial notification within 72 hours of confirmed breach; full forensic report TBD per incident.

6) Suggested BAA language highlights:
   - Definitions: PHI scope, permitted uses, and minimum necessary standard.
   - Security Controls: encryption, access controls, breach notification, audit rights.
   - Data return/deletion: our standard is secure deletion within 30 days of contract termination; we can discuss accelerated timelines.
   - Right to audit: provide SOC 2 and on-site audit coordination for Dedicated customers (reasonable notice).

If Legal pushes for shorter deletion windows or on-prem logging guarantees, Private deployments are the fastest path to satisfy them. Happy to join a technical call with NorthStar.

-Rishi
Director, Infrastructure Security
From: Eliza Hoover <eliza.hoover@northstar-health.com>

Subject: Re: HIPAA / BAA — Redwood eligibility and PHI handling

Marissa — thanks for the quick response and Rishi for the thorough technical notes. A couple of follow-ups from Legal: 

- We reviewed the BAA and submitted a redlined PDF (NorthStar_BAA_Redlined_0315.pdf); we prefer a 15-day turnaround on execution if possible.
- Please confirm: are there any hosted logs (application or infrastructure) that might transiently contain request/response bodies in plain text for debugging or crash reports? We need explicit confirmation that such logs will be disabled or redacted when PHI is in scope.
- Can you confirm the exact deletion SLA (you mentioned 30 days) and whether NorthStar can request immediate purge and attestation on demand?
- We also need a DocuSign path for quick execution; if you can initiate that we’ll push Legal on our side.

Assuming these items are clarified, Legal is comfortable proceeding with Dedicated or Private. We’d like to schedule the technical call — Tue or Wed next week (Mar 23/24) works.

Eliza Hoover
Director of Vendor Risk — NorthStar Health

eliza.hoover@northstar-health.com
